newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - May 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - May 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on
Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not
- The Sindh provincial government has decided to levy a farm tax from July 1, 1998, expecting to raise 200 million rupees.
- Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub left for Washington to hold discussions with United States officials.
- Pakistan's Council of Islamic Ideology has recommended public whipping of drug pushers in the country.
- Bank borrowing by the government reached 96 billion rupees in the second week of May against a full year target of 40 billion rupees.
- A United States justice department task force looking into fund-raising abuses during the 1996 U.S. election is seeking to question ousted Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
- A Taleban official in Kabul showed journalists a container he said contained the radioactive metal Uranium.
- The minister for water and power ruled out the termination of power purchase agreement with the Hub Power Co as threatened by the state-run Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA).
- Pakistan does not face any threat of default in repayment of foreign loans by December nor has it been refused further assistance by the donors, finance minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- The state-run WAPDA is facing serious financial crisis and may default on payments to oil and gas companies, analysts said.

- Major international oil marketing companies are entering the Pakistani market following the decision of the government to deregulate the downstream petroleum products marketing sector for a transitional period of 16 months starting March 1, 1997.
